title: Locked scenario, schema version 1
description: One locked workflow scenario (tests/scenarios/<id>.yaml) or Web API test (tests/acceptance/api/<id>.yaml). Both use this schema and are read by the gate's trusted runner, run_workflow.py (plan 5.8, decision D4). Written in the part of YAML the gate reads (factory-gates lcp/simple_yaml.py): no {} mappings, no | or > text, quote dates and anything starting with a special character. The rules this schema cannot express are in locked-scenarios.md, section 'What the schema cannot check'.

schema_version.description: Always 1. A change to this schema that breaks old files raises it.

id.description: The scenario ID. Equals the file name without .yaml. Starts with wf- (workflow scenario) or api- (Web API test), or ho-wf- and ho-api- in the held-out set; ends with a two-digit number; at most 40 characters.

kind.description: workflow: a flow or classic workflow, run by its own trigger. api: server logic (plug-ins, low-code plug-ins, entity-scoped business rules, columns the server fills in), checked straight after one Web API call.

title.description: One line, in plain words, saying what the scenario shows.

criteria.description: The spec's acceptance criteria this scenario covers, as AC-<n>. The spec's Acceptance Scenario Map lists this scenario's ID against the same criteria.

timeout_seconds.description: How long the runner waits for every expectation to hold before the case fails. Default 300 for workflow, 60 for api.

poll_seconds.description: How often the runner reads Dataverse while it waits. Default 10.

seed.description: Rows the runner creates first, in order, as the set-up. A seed row must not fire the flow or plug-in under test; the trigger is the one act.

trigger.description: The one act the scenario tests.

expect.description: What must be true after the trigger. Rows and plug-in trace logs decide the case; a run record never does.

alias.description: A short name for a row this scenario creates, used in ref: and ${<alias>.id}. Unique in the file. Not run_tag or today.

logical_name.description: A Dataverse table or column logical name: lower case, with the publisher prefix, for example nwind_orders.

value.description: A column value: text, a number, true or false, null, or ref: <alias> for a lookup to a row this scenario created. A choice takes its number; a date takes quoted ISO text. Text may hold ${run_tag}, ${<alias>.id}, ${today}, ${today+N} or ${today-N}.

tag_column.description: The text column, at least 100 characters long and filterable, where the runner writes the run tag. Do not also set it in fields.

oneOf.description: Create a row. The row can be referred to by its alias afterwards.
Update a row this scenario created.
Delete a row this scenario created.
POST to a cloud flow's HTTP trigger, restricted to the Test identity (plan 5.9). The runner finds the trigger's address from the flow's ID. Untested.

row_expect.description: Either a row this scenario created (ref), or the rows a filter finds (filter and table), for example a row the flow made.

filter.description: An OData $filter on the table, which may hold placeholders, for example _nwind_orderid_value eq ${order.id}.

count.description: With filter: how many rows it must find. Default 1. 0 means none may exist.

cleanup.description: With filter: delete the rows it finds when the scenario ends. Default true, because rows a flow makes carry no run tag.

checks.description: Column checks. Every check on every row found must hold.

check.description: One or more of: equals (exact value; for a lookup, the row ID, for example "${customer.id}"), empty (true: no value; false: has a value), contains (text holds it), matches (text matches this regular expression).

run_expect.description: A secondary signal only (plan 5.9): the run of this flow or classic workflow after the trigger. A run record not found is unknown and does not decide the case; one found with another status fails it.

trace_expect.description: Plug-in trace logs written after the trigger, by plug-in type name. Needs plug-in trace logging on in the Test environment.

no_exception.description: Default true: no log found may hold exception details.
